turns.excerpt: Excerpt 3 — The Quiet Mechanics of Conversation People often imagine conversations as exchanges of information, although very little information actually changes hands. More commonly, each remark adjusts the conditions under which the next remark becomes possible. This is why misunderstandings rarely begin with dramatic errors. They usually emerge from small assumptions that remain unexamined because every subsequent sentence quietly accepts them. By the time disagreement becomes visible, its foundations have already settled beyond immediate correction.
